dialogues.speaker: Vitruvius
dialogues.text: Finally. Now, I don't have to wonder who that sand in my mouth used to be.

dialogues.speaker: Vitruvius
dialogues.text: I suppose my era comes slightly after Josephus'. You're familiar with him, aren't you?

dialogues.speaker: Vitruvius
dialogues.text: Still, the history in between remains largely the same. To think that a whole generation could slip by without a single meaningful change...

dialogues.speaker: Vitruvius
dialogues.text: Looking at it that way, my era is nothing more than a Temple of Space, albeit one where everyone grows old.

dialogues.speaker: Vitruvius
dialogues.text: That said, my social standing is far superior to his. After all, I had a spot reserved for me in the cemetery of Irminsul trees.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do you have any legendary accomplishments?

dialogues.speaker: Vitruvius
dialogues.text: Actually, the golden ratio for the human figure in fine arts... I was the one who performed those calculations.

dialogues.speaker: Vitruvius
dialogues.text: Somewhere down the line, though, the "Vitruvian Form" became "Vitruvius's Form."

dialogues.speaker: Vitruvius
dialogues.text: Now, countless generations actually believe I was the naked model for that sketch. I've had painters from the later generations walk up to me, look me up and down, and say, "You know, your physique isn't all that impressive."

dialogues.speaker: Vitruvius
dialogues.text: To which I reply, "Because it was never meant to be me!"
